newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberian senate to define status of peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: Liberian senate to define status of peacekeepers.

text.p: Liberia's new senate debated two first bills on Tuesday, one of them defining the status of African peacekeepers policing the war-ravaged state since 1990.

Senate majority leader Charles Burmskin told reporters the bills on the constitution and the 10,500-strong West African force, ECOMOG, would be presented to new President Charles Taylor later in the day.

The 26-member Senate and a 64-seat lower house also scheduled joint confirmation hearings on Tuesday for about 20 ministers and other executive officials appointed by Taylor since his landslide victory in July 19 elections.

The first bill seeks to reaffirm the authority of Liberia's constitution, some of whose provisions have recently been subjugated to regional accords on ending a seven-year civil war which started in December 1989.
The bill on ECOMOG will spell out the role of the Nigerian-led force, sent to Liberia by the 16-nation Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in 1990.
Details of the draft bill were not available.
ECOMOG got sucked into faction fighting. But last year it received a revised mandate from regional leaders under which it disarmed guerrillas and provided security for the elections.
But the mandate legally ends six months after the installation of the new government, when it should have restructured and retrained Liberia's military and police forces.

Taylor, who took office last Saturday, said in February that he wanted ECOMOG to stay 12 or 18 months longer. But he would prefer a redefined mandate placing the force under the aurthority of the Liberian president.
Any new decision on the future of the force will have to be taken by a full ECOWAS summit later this month or early September, regional officials said.
